title: Germany news: Emergency at Leipzig airport sparked by novice driver
summary: Two men breached a fence at the Leipzig/Halle airport while practicing for a driving test. Meanwhile, the "Invest in Germany Summit" is set to kick off as the government looks to fill gaps in public…

image.caption: Leipzig/Halle airport was already on high alert after bomb-laden drones were discovered there in AugustImage: Tobias Junghannß/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Novice driver caused fence breach at Leipzig/Halle airport: Police

blocks.caption: The breach in the fence triggered a major police operationImage: Erik-Holm Langhof/EHL Media/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Two men have admitted to breaking through a fence at Leipzig/Halle airport while one of them was practicing for a driving test, an incident that triggered a major security operation, police said on Monday.
The two, aged 20 and 32, handed themselves in to the police on Sunday evening, following the incident. The broken fence was first discovered by airport staff late on Saturday.
Police said the 20-year-old had been at the wheel despite not having a valid license.
An investigation was opened into the learner driver for fleeing the scene after breaking through the fence.
The mass-circulation Bild newspaper reported that the car involved, of which fragments were found at the site, was an Audi.
The airport was the site of a security scare in August, when an explosives-laden drone was found there near Ukrainian cargo planes.
German officials accused Russia of having planned an attack, something Moscow denied.
